subject: GreenLine discovery -> model fit proposal + urgent pin request
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@greenlineanalytics.com>
Cc: Nina Patel <nina.patel@greenlineanalytics.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + recommended eval plan and model suggestions

Hi Alex / Nina,

Great to meet you both on the call — thanks for walking through GreenLine's credit-risk scoring workflow. Below is a short recap, recommended next steps, and the models/eval plan we'd like to run against your sample set.

Recap (one-liner): you need an embedding + generative pipeline for customer dispute summarization and risk-scoring enrichment with strict latency targets (p95 < 220ms) and auditability for regulated workflows.

Recommended models for initial fit testing (we'll run side-by-side):
- rw-reasoner-7b-v2.0 (quantized int8) — good balance of recall on numeric extraction and deterministic summarization
- rw-slim-3b-v1.1 — lower-cost baseline to measure unit economics and latency
- rw-embed-1-256 for retrieval/semantic features

What we'll run this week:
1) Sanity benchmarks: latency and token-cost using your sample (we'll post a spreadsheet).
2) Quality evaluation: we will run the prompt_set_v1.jsonl (attached) plus a small golden set you send and produce metrics (F1 for extraction, BLEU/ROUGE for summaries, and a small human spot-check).
3) Regression watch: we'll capture model hashes and will recommend pinning during your integration if any model update changes outputs.

Attachments included: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (prompt + eval harness), greenline_benchmarks_q2.xlsx (template), discovery_recording.mp4 (call recording).

Next steps / asks:
- Please upload a representative sample (200–500 rows) to the Drive link above or reply to this thread with user_samples.csv.
- Approve us to run a short eval on that sample (we'll anonymize and delete afterwards).
- If ok, I'll loop Aditya (engineer) for a technical deep-dive and Soojin for onboarding/PS scheduling.

Proposed timeline: run initial eval within 48 hours of sample receipt; deliver a short scorecard and recommended model for pilot.

Thanks —
Priya

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-06-01T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick recap + recommended eval plan and model suggestions

Priya / team / Alex,

I ran a targeted diff between rw-reasoner-7b-v2.0 and the most recent rollout (rw-reasoner-7b-v2.1) on the GreenLine sample (user_samples.csv). Findings:
- Delta summary length: v2.1 outputs are ~18% shorter on average.
- Extraction recall for invoice numbers / numeric tokens dropped ~5.8% absolute (F1 delta ~ -0.058) on our golden set derived from your sample.
- The change appears tied to a decoding tweak in v2.1 that favors brevity.

Risk assessment: for GreenLine's pipeline the extraction recall drop is material (downstream matching precision falls). I recommend we pin to rw-reasoner-7b-v2.0 for the pilot and run a controlled canary of v2.1 later after we collect more gold labels.

Immediate actions I propose (priority order):
1) Pin GreenLine's preview route to rw-reasoner-7b-v2.0 (we can do application-level route pin via the API config).
2) Open an Ops ticket to schedule a canary window: deploy v2.1 to 5% of traffic for 24 hours with metric collection (recall/latency/cost).
3) Produce a short regression_diff_log.txt with the example pairs and metrics (attaching).
4) Draft a one-page customer note explaining why we pinned and the plan to validate v2.1 safely.

If everyone agrees I can create the pin and the canary ticket within the hour; we should notify Alex/Nina that outputs will match historical behavior while we validate.

Attachment: regression_diff_log.txt (TXT, ~28KB)

—Aditya
